claims.quote: We find that after 500B tokens, an otherwise equivalent MoE trained from scratch already catches up with the upcycled model
claims.reason: Authors state this as their finding that challenges prior upcycling results. The ablation is controlled: Fig. 8 and the body compare upcycling vs an otherwise equivalent from-scratch MoE under the same config for the same additional token budget (610B; catch-up by 500B), with downstream metrics (HellaSwag, MMLU Var), not only loss. The 2T dense checkpoint is the upcycling intervention itself, not an unmatched size/data confound, so this is YES rather than PARTIAL.

Not a novelty claim. The intro only says their experiments show a ~2× training-time speedup; §4.1.1 explicitly attributes similar 2–4× / 2.6× / 2–7× MoE speed-ups to prior work (Artetxe, MoMa, Arctic, Switch). It is a confirmatory measurement, not an ARCH/TRAIN contribution they state as new, first, or key. Drop it.
